sections.title: Negative feedback
sections.text: Negative feedback subtracts the measured output from the reference to form an error signal. Stability still depends on the plant and controller; negative feedback does not guarantee stability.

sections.title: Proportional gain
sections.text: A proportional controller multiplies error by gain Kp. Increasing gain can reduce steady-state error but may increase overshoot.

sections.title: Integral control
sections.text: Integral action accumulates error over time. Actuator saturation can cause windup unless anti-windup is used.

sections.title: Derivative action
sections.text: Derivative action responds to the rate of error change. It is sensitive to measurement noise.
